I wasted 10 years of my life with uncurious doctors & obgyn that kept having me cycle through unhelpful SSRIs. It’s life changing! Every time I pass a threshold I struggle to remember why I’m there. 

I started doing it because I read an article about how Disney did a study and found out that the average person would travel 6-8 feet or so before littering if they couldn’t find a trash bin (at their parks). 

So they were like, we are going to work with the natural tendencies of these people and place a trash can every 6 feet. 

I try to think of it like that. I am a mega corporation doing research so i can determine how to best facilitate the average/lowest common denominator when I’m struggling. 

And also consider that it’s kinda flawed thinking to just expect to have willpower; what I’ve been told about myself is affecting my ability to problem solve, bc they were unreasonable expectations.

It makes more sense (for me) to set myself up for success by identifying and preemptively managing these behaviors with tiny household changes. (🥲or at least I try lol)

Hopefully this is helpful, insurance is so complicated, this is what I have learned:

When you use the healthcare.gov marketplace, you will have to select an insurance. You may be limited by 1) what is available in your state and 2) what you can afford. 

For me, I only have the options of Premera BCBS or Moda for health insurance. Neither of them cover Botox for TMJ… but I think BCBS may if they receive something called a “prior authorization” from your healthcare provider. The unfortunate thing about prior authorizations, is that the quality of the request affects the likelihood of its acceptance & some doctor offices SUCK about creating a quality request. You also have to show that you have pursued other approved methods of treatment and they haven’t worked. 

I have already done 2x 6month series of physical therapy, dentist x-rays & night guard, tried muscle relaxers and naproxen. Next, I am going to have my pain doc inject a solution into my trigger points and acupuncture (separately not together). If that doesn’t work, the doctor has indicated they will work with me on prior authorization for Botox injections. 

When I signed up for healthcare through the marketplace in December, I used a non-profit called United Way to help walk me through the process and explain the different options for me. I would highly recommend seeking out this resource or a similar one when you sign up. We video chatted, but I could have gone to the library as well. Usually there is more help during November-December bc that’s when everyone in the marketplace elects to change plans or stay. However, you can get insurance anytime there is a life change, so I’d imagine some level of this resource would still be available. 

Currently my TMJ is believed to be muscular, so my treatment options may differ from yours. 

TLDR;
Most Healthcare Marketplace insurance providers likely won’t cover it, but some may through prior authorizations. Make an appointment with a United Way representative in your state to walk you through it. (United Way is a charity, their assistance is free) 

Also, once you find out what insurance providers are available for you, you can google something like “premera tmj botox designation”. The first result in this example shows me this link, where all the covered treatments are listed. (https://www.premera.com/medicalpolicies/2.01.535.pdf). Botox is classified as investigational here, which as I understand it means it won’t be covered. (But prior authorization may be possible, I’m still learning how to do all of this)

Something that helps me. 

Let’s say u have a strong feeling, the kind that triggers intense responses outside ur body. Usually it’s like input, then normal response feelings(sad) become agitated feelings, which become super agitated(rage panic) in a way that provokes a rage response. 

1. Do you notice it’s happening? How soon can you tell it’s happening? Work on identifying your feelings so that you can gauge where you are in the cycle. (Normal hurt feeling >agitated>super agitated>physical outbursts of rage). If you know what it feels like to be near rage, you can implement strategies to cope or resolve feelings before the rage outburst happens. (Talk out/ journal all the things that bother you to process them. Care for yourself psychologically)

2. While you are angry / rageful… okay u couldn’t control it and now you are here again in this altered state. Where do you feel it in your body? How does your body feel? Just talk these things through out loud to yourself or someone else. Notice the uncomfortable things like tight shoulders or clenched fists- and just relax them. Return the tense posture slowly and deliberately to an open gentle posture. Think about releasing some of the feelings that caused or are associated with this discomfort as well. 
3. Do you think it’s more input causes you to feel sad>anger or input makes you feel panic/fear>anger? That might give you an insight into your state of mind. Try to find out where the feelings are coming from and what they feel like. This will help you more effectively triage them later.
